node.statement: Let arbitrary C>0, eta_0>0, and beta>1/2 be given. All three numbers 1/(2*sqrt(2)), sqrt(eta_0/2), and (C*2^beta)^(-1/(2*beta-1)) are positive, so choose 0<lambda strictly below their minimum, and set eta:=eta_lambda=2*lambda^2 and Q:=Q_lambda as in 1.1. The first cutoff gives lambda<1/2 and eta<1/4; the second gives eta<eta_0; hence 0<eta<min{eta_0,1/4}. By 1.2, Q is row-stochastic and ||Q^2-Q||<=eta. Since 2*beta-1>0, the third strict cutoff implies C*2^beta*lambda^(2*beta)<lambda. By 1.3, every stochastic idempotent E satisfies ||Q-E||>=lambda, while C*eta^beta=C*(2*lambda^2)^beta=C*2^beta*lambda^(2*beta)<lambda; thus every such E satisfies ||Q-E||>C*eta^beta. Finally, a uniform replacement exponent beta>1/2 would mean that some fixed C>0 and eta_0>0 work in every dimension for every row-stochastic Q of defect at most eta<=eta_0, producing a stochastic idempotent E with ||Q-E||<=C*eta^beta. Applying the just-constructed dimension-four witness to those proposed C and eta_0 gives the literal contradiction that every E has ||Q-E||>C*eta^beta. Therefore no uniform beta>1/2 can replace 1/2.
